name: decode-negative-count-wraps
why: converts a negative count to size_t, which wraps to a huge reserve.

name: decode-no-reserve
why: correct, but grows by repeated reallocation (fails the Fast tier).

edits.old: out.reserve(total);  // one allocation instead of repeated growth

name: decode-off-by-one
why: emits count + 1 copies of each value.

name: encode-compares-with-first-run
why: compares with the FIRST run instead of the last one.

name: encode-new-run-count-zero
why: a new run starts with count 0, so every run is one short.

name: make-buffer-uses-resize
why: resize creates n elements, so the vector is not empty.

edits.old: v.reserve(n);  // reserve changes the capacity; resize would change the size

name: remove-evens-copies
why: builds a second vector and copies it back (allocates; fails the Fast tier).

edits.old: std::erase_if(v, [](int x) { return x % 2 == 0; });  // the erase-remove idiom, in one call

name: remove-evens-erase-in-loop
why: erases inside an iterator loop: skips elements and uses an invalidated iterator.

edits.old: std::erase_if(v, [](int x) { return x % 2 == 0; });  // the erase-remove idiom, in one call

name: remove-evens-wrong-parity-test
why: tests x % 2 != 1, which also removes negative odd numbers.

edits.old: std::erase_if(v, [](int x) { return x % 2 == 0; });  // the erase-remove idiom, in one call
edits.new: std::erase_if(v, [](int x) { return x % 2 != 1; });  // the erase-remove idiom, in one call

name: squares-int-overflow
why: multiplies in int before widening, so large squares overflow.

edits.old: out.push_back(static_cast<long long>(i) * i);  // widen BEFORE multiplying: i * i overflows int

name: squares-no-reserve
why: correct, but grows by repeated reallocation (fails the Fast tier).
